questions.def: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb.
questions.question: She eats ___ lunch at noon.

questions.def: Never is used after 'have' to express absence of experience.
questions.question: I have ___ been to Japan.

questions.def: Past simple 'studied' correctly describes completed action.
questions.question: He (study) ___ hard for the exam.

questions.def: Often is placed before the main verb in questions.
questions.question: Do you ___ go to the gym?

questions.def: 'Just' goes between 'have' and the past participle.
questions.question: I ___ finished my work.

questions.def: Past simple 'arrived' shows a completed action in the past.
questions.question: They (arrive) ___ late last night.

questions.def: Sometimes is used to express frequency.
questions.question: He ___ goes to the library on Sundays.

questions.def: Already goes between 'have' and the past participle.
questions.question: I ___ seen that movie.

questions.def: Past simple 'spoke' describes a completed action.
questions.question: She (speak) ___ quietly in the library.

questions.def: Rarely is an adverb of frequency.
questions.question: I ___ visit my grandparents.

questions.def: Adverb goes after the verb 'to be'.
questions.question: They ___ late for the meeting.

questions.def: Present simple 'drives' describes a habitual action.
questions.question: He (drive) ___ carefully on the highway.

questions.def: Never is used to express lack of a recurring action.
questions.question: We ___ go to that restaurant anymore.

questions.def: Adverb goes after 'is' but before the past participle.
questions.question: She ___ to the party.

questions.def: Present simple 'work' describes a habitual action.
questions.question: They (work) ___ hard every day.

questions.def: Occasionally is an adverb of frequency.
questions.question: They ___ visit us.

questions.def: Adverb goes after the verb 'to be'.
questions.question: He ___ on time.

questions.def: Past simple 'sang' describes a completed action.
questions.question: She (sing) ___ beautifully at the concert.

questions.def: Always is an adverb of frequency.
questions.question: He ___ forgets his keys.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb.
questions.question: We ___ to the beach.

questions.def: Present perfect 'have eaten' shows action completed at unspecified time.
questions.question: I (eat) ___ lunch already.

questions.def: 'Fully' correctly modifies 'understand' as an adverb.
questions.question: I ___ understand the instructions.

questions.def: 'Just' goes between 'has' and the past participle.
questions.question: He ___ his homework.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency (like 'often') usually go before the main verb.
questions.question: She visits her family ___.

questions.def: 'Already' is used to say something has happened sooner than expected.
questions.question: I have ___ finished my homework.

questions.def: Adverbs modify verbs and are often formed by adding '-ly'.
questions.question: She ___ ran to the store.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency typically come before the main verb.
questions.question: They ___ go to the beach in summer.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb (except 'be').
questions.question: I ___ go there anymore.

questions.def: Adverbs modify verbs and show how the action is performed.
questions.question: He ___ drives his car.

questions.def: 'Never' is an adverb of frequency indicating zero times.
questions.question: I ___ go to the gym on Sundays.
